key_insight: Low voltage-estimation errors do not necessarily imply physically feasible or operationally reliable ANN power-flow solutions under system shifts.
engineering_relevance: Evaluating physical consistency alongside accuracy can better inform the deployment of ANN power-flow solvers as grid topology and load distributions change.
method: Assess voltage errors alongside KCL gaps, branch-flow gaps, and KVL residuals.
Measure continuous feasibility scores and strict, practical, and relaxed power-flow feasibility rates.
Test topology shifts, mixed-topology training, load-distribution shifts, and combined shifts.
evidence_signal: Eight ANN architectures, including graph-input models, load-only baselines, and physics-informed neural networks, are evaluated consistently across four case studies, revealing accuracy–feasibility mismatches particularly under combined shifts.
watch_item: The abstract provides no numerical feasibility rates or acceptance thresholds, limiting assessment of deployment readiness.
paper_title: Beyond Accuracy: Physics-Informed Evaluation of ANN-based Power Flow Solvers under System Shift
